question.text: As of 26 November 2026, will Russia be listed among the teams in the IIHF's official field for the 2027 IIHF U18 Women's World Championship?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves based on the IIHF's own official tournament pages for the 2027 IIHF U18 Women's World Championship (Ostrava, Czechia, 8–16 January 2027) as they stand at 23:59 UTC on 26 November 2026. It resolves YES if a team representing Russia — listed as "Russia"/"RUS" or under a neutral designation such as "ROC" or "AIN" — appears either in the participating-teams list on the official event page (https://www.iihf.com/en/events/2027/ww18) or in at least one game on the official competition schedule (https://www.iihf.com/en/events/2027/ww18/schedule). It resolves NO if no such team appears on either page at that time. For reference, as of 13 November 2026 both pages list eight teams (Canada, Czechia, Germany, Hungary, Switzerland, Slovakia, Sweden, United States) and a 21-game schedule containing no Russian team; the question asks whether that changes by the resolution cutoff.
question.fine_print: If the IIHF pages cannot be loaded at resolution time, or if resolution is checked after the cutoff, the resolver will use the Internet Archive (web.archive.org) captures of the event page and of the schedule page that are closest to, and not later than, 23:59 UTC on 26 November 2026; if no such capture exists for a page, [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) reporting the tournament field as of that time will be used. If the IIHF relocates the tournament or republishes the field for the same 2027 IIHF U18 Women's World Championship at a different URL, that official page governs. A slot left as a placeholder (e.g., "TBD") or an entry not identified as Russian does not count as Russia being listed. An IIHF news article, press statement or media report that Russia will or will not play does not by itself resolve the question; the outcome is determined solely by whether a Russian team appears in the field or schedule on those pages.

research:
## Russia and the 2027 IIHF U18 Women's World Championship field: research as of 16 November 2026

Short version: I found nothing that adds Russia to the Ostrava field. On 15 November the IIHF kept Russia out of the World Juniors because Canada will not let Russian players in. Czechia has taken the same visa position for Ostrava. But I found no IIHF decision that is specific to the U18 women's event.

### 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-16: I could not load either official page. The event page and the schedule page both returned HTTP 403 to my direct fetch. The pages are built by scripts, and I found no underlying data file I could read. [event](https://www.iihf.com/en/events/2027/ww18) / [schedule](https://www.iihf.com/en/events/2027/ww18/schedule)
- 2026-10-09: This is the most recent Wayback capture of the schedule page, so it predates the CAS ruling. The resolver may need a fresh capture or credible reports. [archive](http://web.archive.org/web/20261009105726/https://www.iihf.com/en/events/2027/ww18/schedule)
- 2026-11-05: iSport (Czech) published the field and schedule without Russia:
  - Group A: Germany, Switzerland, Sweden, USA.
  - Group B: Czechia, Canada, Hungary, Slovakia.
  - It shows no revised schedule and does not mention Germany being replaced.
  - This matches the question's status check of 13 November (8 teams, 21 games). [iSport](https://isport.blesk.cz/clanek/hokej-reprezentace-ms-v-hokeji-do-18-let/481811/ms-v-hokeji-zen-u18-2027-ostrava-program-skupiny-cesky-prijede-rusko.html)

### 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. I found no IIHF announcement about the U18 women's event since the CAS ruling. I also found no report of a revised Ostrava schedule that includes Russia.
- The closest precedent points against Russia being added. On 15 November the IIHF Council excluded Russia from the World Juniors, citing restrictions that the host government had "formally communicated." Czechia has taken the equivalent visa position for Ostrava.

### 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-15/16: The IIHF confirmed Russia's U20 team cannot play at the World Juniors in Edmonton and Red Deer (26 December to 5 January).
  - It said it had considered alternative arrangements before keeping Canada as host.
  - An updated World Juniors and U20 Division I Group A schedule is to be posted.
  - None of the coverage I found mentions the U18 women's event. [Ukrainska Pravda](https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2026/11/15/8062987/), [CBC](https://www.cbc.ca/sports/hockey/iihf-world-juniors-russia-not-competing-9.7422880), [ESPN](https://www.espn.com/olympics/story/_/id/50373148/russia-not-allowed-world-juniors-boycott-looms)
- 2026-11-15: The Russian federation called the decision "unlawful." It says the IIHF's force majeure reasoning is unfounded and plans to appeal to the IOC with the Russian Olympic Committee. [Champion.com.ua](https://champion.com.ua/ukr/ice-hockey/rosiya-zvernetsya-do-mok-cherez-nedopusk-na-molodizhniy-chs-2027-1090952/), [EssentiallySports](https://www.essentiallysports.com/olympics-news-ice-hockey-russia-vows-legal-action-against-iihf-after-two-zero-two-seven-world-junior-championships-snub/)
- 2026-11-14: Federations in Canada, Sweden, Finland, Germany, Czechia and Latvia say they will not play Russia, and some sponsors are threatening to pull out. Euronews repeats that Czech authorities will not issue visas for Ostrava. [Euronews](https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/14/russia-urges-iihf-to-move-canada-world-juniors-as-hockey-boycotts-spread)
- Early to mid November (exact date not confirmed):
  - Ostrava's new mayor, Richard Vereš, said it is "not possible" for Russian players to come to Ostrava. [Deník](https://moravskoslezsky.denik.cz/zpravy-region/veres-primator-ostrava-hokej-mistrovstvi-sveta-rusko-valka-ukrajina-spor-iihf-macinka-vyrok/)
  - The Czech federation has reportedly considered giving up hosting rights. [Tiscali](https://www.tiscali.cz/ms-v-hokeji-se-rozpada-pred-ocima-sest-zemi-bojkotuje-turnaj-kvuli-rusku-skoda-auto-hrozi-stazenim-sponzorstvi-799922)
- About 2026-11-02/03: Czechia announced it will not grant visas to the Russian U18 women's team. Daily Faceoff reports that if Russia did play, Germany, the lowest-ranked team, would be removed to make room. [Daily Faceoff](https://www.dailyfaceoff.com/news/czechia-wont-grant-visa-russia-womens-team-upcoming-iihf-u18-womens-world-championship-ban-news)

### 4. Base rates
- Russia has not appeared in the field of any IIHF championship since February 2022.
- Since the CAS ruling, the only case decided so far is the World Juniors. There, the IIHF first sent federations a schedule with Russia in place of Norway. It then excluded Russia anyway once the host government formally refused entry. I found no case where the public IIHF pages listed Russia after the CAS ruling.
- Ostrava differs in one way: the event moving elsewhere is less of a concern than with the World Juniors. Czechia has openly discussed handing back the event, but the question says a relocated official page would still count.

### 5. Other forecasts
- None of the supplied Kalshi or Polymarket markets match this question. The Polymarket IIHF 2027 champion market is unrelated.
- I found no Metaculus or Manifold question on this, and no expert forecast.

### 6. Upcoming events before 26 November
- An IIHF Council decision specific to the U18 women's event. The World Juniors logic, host-government restrictions, would apply directly to Czechia.
- Any official Czech government notification to the IIHF. For the World Juniors, a formal notification from Canada was the trigger.
- The Russian appeal to the IOC and any new CAS filing. Neither is likely to produce a ruling within 10 days.
- Any change to the IIHF pages, such as Germany being swapped for Russia or a ninth slot. Also, a new Wayback capture before the cutoff, since the latest one is from 9 October.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) About 10 days remain, until 23:59 UTC on 26 November 2026. For Yes, a Russian team (RUS, ROC, AIN or similar) has to appear on the official IIHF U18 Women's event page or in at least one game on its schedule at the cutoff, including on any relocated official page.

(b) If nothing changes, the answer is No. As of 13 November both pages show eight teams and 21 games, none involving Russia.

(c) Base rate: Russia has appeared in no IIHF championship field since February 2022. Since the CAS ruling there is one comparable case, a host government refusing visas, at the World Juniors. Russia did not end up in the published field there, so the record is 0 of 1. The base rate for Russia being added within a 10-day window is roughly 5% or less.

(d) Evidence:
- For Yes:
  - On 30 October, CAS explicitly ordered the IIHF to admit Russia to this event.
  - Around 8 November, the IIHF circulated an adjusted World Juniors schedule containing Russia, which shows it is willing to rewrite programmes.
  - Russia is applying legal and political pressure: an IOC appeal, demands to relocate events, and threats of sanctions.
- For No:
  - On 15 November, the IIHF Council excluded Russia from the World Juniors, citing restrictions the host government had formally communicated. It also chose not to relocate that event.
  - Around 2 November, Czechia stated it will refuse visas for Ostrava. The prime minister, interior minister, sports minister and the Ostrava mayor have all said so.
  - The Czech federation refuses to play Russia, and the tournament is about seven weeks away.
  - No revised Ostrava schedule containing Russia has been reported.

(e) Scenarios:
- No: The IIHF applies the World Juniors logic to Ostrava, either through a formal decision or by simply leaving the pages unchanged, and the field stays at eight teams through 26 November.
- Yes: The IIHF, under CAS enforcement pressure, publishes a revised Ostrava schedule that swaps Russia for Germany, perhaps temporarily before a force majeure ruling. Alternatively, it moves the event to a visa-issuing host such as Slovakia and lists Russia there, all before the cutoff.

(f) I start from a base rate of about 5%. The 15 November World Juniors decision is a direct precedent applying almost identical facts, and it pushes the estimate down. A small residual covers the chance of a page update or relocation, and the resolver's reliance on archives adds some noise. I end at about 3%.

Probability: 3%

**(a) Time left and what Yes requires.** There are about 10 days until 23:59 UTC on 26 November 2026. Yes requires a Russian team, under any name including a neutral one, to appear in the team list on the official IIHF event page or in at least one game on the official schedule at that moment.

**(b) Status quo.** As of 13 November the field had 8 teams and 21 games, with no Russia. If nothing changes, the answer is No.

**(c) Base rate.** Russia has appeared in no published IIHF championship field since February 2022. Since the CAS ruling, only one case has been decided: the World Juniors, where the host also refused visas. Russia was briefly placed in a schedule sent to federations, but there is no confirmation it reached the public pages, and on 15 November it was removed. That gives a base rate of about 0 of 1, so roughly 5% or less.

**(d) Strongest evidence.**
- **For Yes:**
  - The CAS order of 30 October explicitly covers this event.
  - The IIHF said on 7 November it was "taking the necessary steps" to implement the ruling.
  - For the World Juniors, an adjusted schedule including Russia was circulated around 8 November, so the IIHF has shown it will at least draft such schedules.
  - The Russian federation is pressing hard and threatening legal action.
- **For No:**
  - On 15 November the IIHF Council excluded Russia from the World Juniors, citing visa restrictions the host government had "formally communicated."
  - Czechia's position is the same:
    - The Prime Minister said on 2 November that no visas would be issued.
    - The Interior Minister cites a 2023 government resolution barring short-stay visas.
    - The Ostrava mayor and the Czech federation are also opposed.
